title: Sharpness-Aware Pretraining Mitigates Catastrophic Forgetting
claim: Our flatness-promoting pretraining preserves base-model capability far better than the standard baseline after diverse downstream modifications.
layout: 2 panels (4 bars plus PTQ), grouped bars, green percentage-reduction arrows
description: A grouped bar chart of pretraining-benchmark accuracy (y-axis, about 39 to 43) after different modifications to the base model. The x-axis lists the post-training datasets MetaMath, StackMathQA, Tülu-3 and MusicPile in the large left panel. A narrower right panel shows 4-bit post-training quantization (PTQ). Each group has two bars. The OLMo baseline is pale blue-gray and SAM is saturated magenta. Two horizontal dashed lines mark the base models' accuracy: dark navy for the baseline and faded pink for SAM. The SAM bars drop less than the baseline bars. Dotted black arrows link each pair of bar tops. Bold green labels give the reduction in forgetting: −31%, −22%, −35%, and −40% for PTQ. MusicPile shows a bold black 0%. The legend at the bottom separates 'Base model' from 'Post-trained'. The eye goes first to the magenta bars and the green percentages.
caption: Main results from OLMo-2-1B experiments. We take an OLMo-2-1B model pretrained on 4T tokens and then mid-train it for 50B tokens using SAM and AdamW. After further modification by SFT (MetaMath, StackMathQA, Tülu-3, and MusicPile) and 4-bit quantization, SAM reduces forgetting on the pretraining eval benchmark.
abstract: Pretraining optimizers are tuned to produce the strongest possible base model, on the assumption that a stronger starting point yields a stronger model after subsequent changes like post-training and quantization. This overlooks the geometry of the base model which controls how much of the base model's capabilities survive subsequent parameter updates. We study three pretraining optimization approaches that bias optimization toward flatter minima: Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM), large learning rates, and shortened learning rate annealing periods. Across model sizes ranging from 20M to 150M parameters, we find that these interventions consistently improve downstream performance after post-training on five common datasets with up to 80% less forgetting. These principles hold at scale: a short SAM mid-training phase applied to an existing OLMo-2-1B checkpoint reduces forgetting by 31% after MetaMath post-training and by 40% after 4-bit quantization.
